title: WZXU FieldQuote Detailed User Guide
text:
WZXU FIELDQUOTE
Detailed
User Guide
A practical operating manual for painting, concrete, and window estimates.
From measurement to customer quote
Set up your business, review your rates, measure each work area, check the price, export the PDF, and protect
your records.
Edition: October 1, 2026
Coverage: current workspace application; new-estimate formula 1.2.0; Windows launcher documentation 1.0.1.
Written for business owners, estimators, and field staff. Button and field names match the inspected application
source.
Accuracy and scope
This guide is based on the app implementation, calculation engine, PDF exporter, storage logic, and Windows
release instructions in the supplied project. It documents current behavior, including limitations that affect everyday
use. Published website features may differ after a later release.
Open WZXU FieldQuote: wzxu-fieldquote.vercel.app

A reliable first quote
1. Open Settings, enter your company information, and select Save company profile.
2. Open Rates, replace the starter values with your actual costs and production assumptions, and select Save rates.
3. On Home, select the Painting, Concrete, or Windows trade card.
4. Complete job details, select Add measurements, and check every work area.
5. Select Review price. Check the price, duration, notes, custom items, and payment terms.
6. Select Create PDF quote, inspect the downloaded file, and send it using your preferred email or messaging app.
7. Update the status yourself and download a JSON backup from Settings.

title: Getting started
text:
USER GUIDE / 02
Getting started
Browser and phone access
Open the app website in the browser you intend to use regularly. The same estimating workflow adapts to desktop
and phone screens. If your browser offers an install or home-screen option, you can use it for easier access; the
exact browser command varies.
Connect to the internet for the first visit and allow the app to finish loading. After the app has been cached, the last
downloaded release and locally saved estimates can work offline. Check that your usual app copy opens while offline
before relying on it at a job site.
Windows installed version
The supplied Windows test release requires Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. Extract the distribution ZIP, run
WZXU-FieldQuote-Setup.exe, and follow the installer. Open the app through its desktop or Start menu shortcut.
Estimates are kept in your Windows user profile under AppData/Roaming/WZXU FieldQuote Desktop. The
supplied uninstall configuration retains this data.
Windows portable version
Extract the ZIP and open Portable/WZXU-FieldQuote.exe. Keep every file in the Portable folder together, including
portable.json. The app creates a Data folder beside the executable. Use a writable folder or drive. Close the app
before copying or moving the entire Portable folder, including Data.
Separate copies have separate records. A browser, the installed Windows app, and the portable Windows app
do not automatically share estimates. Use JSON backup and restore to transfer ordinary records between them.
Navigating and updating
The main tabs are Home, Estimates, Rates, and Settings. During the estimate flow, use the back arrow to revisit
previous screens. The three main stages are Job details, Measure the work, and Review quote.
When Update ready appears, select Save and reload. The app saves pending work before switching releases; it
may apply an update automatically while idle on Home. Website updates and Windows launcher updates are
separate. When replacing portable software, preserve the existing Data folder.

title: Set up company details and rates
text:
USER GUIDE / 03
Set up company details and rates
Company profile
1. Open Settings. Replace the example Business name, Phone, Email, and Address.
2. Select Save company profile. These details appear on customer PDFs. Verify them in an exported PDF before
sending your first real quote.
Payment terms are edited on each quote review screen. The current Settings screen has no payment-terms editor.
New estimates inherit the stored company default, so review the inherited text every time.
Your rates
Visible rate
How to use it
Labor cost ($/hr)
Your internal cost per crew-hour. Use a consistent business costing basis.
Paint allowance and coverage
Paint cost per gallon and coverage in square feet per gallon per coat.
Concrete allowance
Concrete material cost per cubic yard.
Window allowance
Saved default allowance; check the separate Unit allowance on every window estimate.
Paint / concrete production
Square feet per crew-hour. A higher production figure generally reduces calculated
labor time.
Replacement window labor
Base hours per replacement unit, before condition and trim additions.
Overhead and Markup
Percentages applied in sequence to the calculated cost. Markup is different from profit
margin.
Minimum job
Minimum base selling subtotal before any custom items or manual override.
Select Save rates after editing. Saving marks starter rates as reviewed; it does not prove accuracy against completed
jobs. The Home starter-rate notice can remain visible even after saving, so use the Rates screen and the quote rate
snapshot to confirm what is stored.
Saved rate snapshots: changing Rates affects new estimates. Existing estimates and duplicates keep their
saved snapshot. There is no visible command to apply the latest rate book to an old quote. Start a new estimate
when you need current rates.

title: Create the job and work areas
text:
USER GUIDE / 04
Create the job and work areas
Job details
1. On Home, choose the required trade. New estimate starts Painting; use the Concrete or Windows card for those
trades.
2. Enter Customer name, contact details, Project title, Job address, City, State, and ZIP. Use a specific title such as
"Living room and hallway repaint".
3. Check Quote expires. New quotes default to roughly 30 days ahead and State defaults to CA; change both where
needed.
4. Select Add measurements. Replace the populated example dimensions and conditions before using the
calculated result.
More than one room, slab, or window group
Each estimate contains work areas for its selected trade. The initial tab is Primary area. Select an area tab before
changing its inputs; each tab keeps its own measurements and conditions.
Control
Behavior
Add area
Creates another area with zero core dimensions or quantity. Other defaults may remain;
check every condition.
Duplicate area
Copies the selected area, including measurements and options. Change anything that
differs and check for double counting.
Remove
Removes the selected area when more than one area exists. Review the remaining
totals afterward.
Review price
Recalculates the saved cost, duration, measurements, and customer scope groups
from the work areas.
The current workflow adds areas within a single trade. Create separate estimates for separate trades. Area names
are generated by the app; the current screen has no rename control. Identify locations in Project title and Customer
notes as needed.
Saving and revising
Estimate edits autosave locally after a short delay. Avoid closing immediately after typing. To revise a saved quote,
open it in Estimates, use the back arrow to reach measurements or job details, make changes, and select Review
price again to refresh the saved pricing and scope before export.
The live measurement panel responds immediately. Returning through Review price is the step that writes the
recalculated breakdown and scope to the quote.

title: Painting: enter the right surface
text:
USER GUIDE / 05
Painting: enter the right surface
Choose surface and measurement method
Select Interior walls, Ceiling, Trim, Doors, Cabinets, or Exterior surface. For walls or ceilings, choose Room / surface
dimensions or Known paintable area. Trim, doors, and cabinets use known paintable area. Paint grade offers
Economy, Standard, and Premium; these change the paint-material allowance.
Field / option
Meaning and effect
Length, Width, Height
Feet. Interior wall area is 2 x (length + width) x height. Ceiling-only area is length x
width.
Openings
Combined square feet of doors and windows, not their count. Deduction applies when
Deduct doors and windows is on in dimension mode.
Known paintable area
Net surface area before coats. The app uses the entered area directly; perform any
opening deductions yourself.
Coats
Multiplies base surface area for paint usage and application labor.
Include ceiling
Adds length x width to wall area in dimension mode. Avoid also adding a duplicate
ceiling area.
Surface preparation
Light, Standard, or Heavy changes prep labor.
Occupied / furniture present
Increases calculated application labor.
Trim length / Doors / Cabinet
faces
Adds detail labor to the area calculation. These counts do not independently create
paint gallons.
Production factor
Multiplies application labor. Above 1 increases hours; the engine floors the factor at 0.5.
Gallons override
A positive value replaces calculated paint gallons for material costing. Zero or blank
removes this override.
Important measuring distinctions
Known area is the surface to be painted, not floor area and not the area already multiplied by coats. For a single
exterior face or an irregular surface, use measured net paintable area; the room-dimension method assumes a
perimeter calculation.
For trim, doors, and cabinets, provide the paintable area as well as relevant detail counts. Detail counts add labor, so
avoid counting the same detail work twice in separate areas. Specify unusual prep, coating systems, access, and
protection in Customer notes.

title: Painting: verify gallons and labor
text:
USER GUIDE / 06
Painting: verify gallons and labor
Worked quantity example
Use one interior-wall area with Length 16 ft, Width 12 ft, Height 9 ft, Openings 42 sq ft, two coats, Deduct doors and
windows on, and Include ceiling off. Assume saved coverage of 350 sq ft/gal/coat and the default 10% waste.
Calculation
Result
Gross wall area: 2 x (16 + 12) x
9
504 sq ft
Net base area: 504 - 42
462 sq ft
Coated area: 462 x 2
924 sq ft
Before rounding: 924 / 350 x
1.10
2.904 gal
Calculated paint, rounded up
3 gal
The area panel shows the base area, coats, coated area, saved coverage, calculated gallons, and any gallons
override. Copy calculation details copies a technical worksheet for review; it is not the customer quote.
How labor differs from gallons
Preparation labor is based on base area. Application labor uses coated area divided by Paint production, then
condition factors. Detail counts add more hours. A gallons override changes material cost but does not replace
measured area or crew-hours.
With the same example, starter production of 155 sq ft/hr, Standard prep, Standard access, occupied conditions,
factor 1, and no details, prep is 462 / 240 = 1.925 hours. Application is 924 / 155 x 1.2 = about 7.154 hours. Total is
about 9.08 crew-hours.
Respond to quantity warnings
Check warnings for zero dimensions, very large measurements, unusually high waste, openings larger than wall
area, tall surfaces, or excessive paint quantity. If the app shows I checked this unusual quantity, verify the
measurements and duplicated areas before switching it on to continue.
Current UI limit: painting waste and access are stored assumptions but have no visible per-estimate controls.
Fresh areas use 10% waste and Standard access. Height above 16 ft can trigger a warning; lift or scaffold costs
are not added automatically. Add a reviewed custom allowance where appropriate.

title: Concrete: measure and price the pour
text:
USER GUIDE / 07
Concrete: measure and price the pour
1. Enter Length and Width in feet and Depth in inches. Use separate areas for different thicknesses or conditions.
2. Choose Broom, Smooth, or Decorative finish and the required Reinforcement type: None, Fiber, Wire mesh, or
Rebar.
3. Enter Forming in linear feet, Setup time in hours, and Equipment charge in dollars. Check Demolition, Excavation /
base prep, Separate base preparation, and Concrete pump as applicable.
4. Review area, cubic yards, crew-hours, and the Extras component on the price review.
Volume example
For a 20 ft x 12 ft slab at 4 inches depth: area = 240 sq ft. Raw concrete = 240 x (4 / 12) / 27 = 2.963 cu yd. With the
default 10% waste, estimated material quantity is 3.26 cu yd after display rounding. The engine prices the unrounded
volume; supplier order increments may differ.
What the current calculation includes
Item
Implementation allowance
Delivery / short load
Stored delivery fee, plus stored short-load fee when calculated volume is below 4 cu yd.
Starter values are $275 and $225 per area calculation.
Reinforcement
Material allowance per sq ft: fiber $0.55, mesh $1.15, rebar $2.40.
Demolition / excavation
Adds labor and area-based extras: demolition $2.20/sq ft; excavation $1.60/sq ft.
Separate base preparation
Adds $1.25/sq ft in addition to other selected options.
Concrete pump
Adds a fixed $650 allowance when selected.
Forming / setup / equipment
Forming adds labor at 24 linear ft/hr; setup adds entered hours; equipment adds the
entered charge.
The Reinforcement type selector takes precedence over the legacy Reinforcement toggle when a type is stored.
Use the selector. Multiple concrete areas can each incur delivery, short-load, and pump allowances. Check
duplication before finalizing.
These are estimating assumptions, not supplier quotes. The screen has no waste, access, or delivery-fee editor.
Confirm unusual depth, large pours, scheduling, supplier charges, and whether both base-prep options describe
distinct work.

title: Windows: group matching units
text:
USER GUIDE / 08
Windows: group matching units
1. Create one area for windows sharing size and conditions. Enter Quantity, Width and Height in inches, and Window
type.
2. Choose Replacement or New opening, Opening condition, and Story. Select removal, trim, haul-away, sealing, and
finish work as needed.
3. Check Unit allowance explicitly. Enter Access equipment and Permit allowance where required. Add another area
for different window groups.
Understand the size-adjusted allowance
Area per unit = width x height / 144. Material allowance = Unit allowance x max(0.8, area per unit / 15) x quantity. The
visible Unit allowance is therefore a base allowance before the size factor, not necessarily the final material cost per
window.
Worked example
Four 36 x 60 inch replacement windows
Area per unit
36 x 60 / 144 = 15 sq ft; size factor = 1.
Material allowance
At $420 entered per unit: 4 x $420 = $1,680.
Base and trim labor
At 3 replacement hours plus 1.25 trim hours each: 17 crew-hours for four units, with
good openings and first-story Standard access.
Removal + disposal + sealing
Using starter fees: 4 x ($85 + $35 + $28) = $592.
Additional choices
Finish work adds $65/unit; entered equipment and permit allowances are added as
extras.
New-opening labor starts at 5 hours per unit. Needs repair adds 1.5 hours per unit; Rebuild opening adds 4. Any story
above 1 adds 1.25 hours per unit. Trim adds 1.25 hours per unit. The current Window type selection does not apply a
separate type-price multiplier.
Check each new window quote: a fresh estimate starts with a Unit allowance of $420. Editing Window allowance
in Rates does not replace this populated field. Enter your intended allowance here. An entered zero produces zero
window material allowance.
Upper-story warnings do not automatically add access equipment. The combined quantity panel can sum per-unit
size figures across areas; use each area's dimensions to verify individual sizes. Confirm supplier specifications and
describe special installation scope in Customer notes.

title: Understand price and duration
text:
USER GUIDE / 09
Understand price and duration
Price calculation order
The engine estimates Labor, Materials, and Extras for every area. It combines these direct costs, applies Overhead,
applies Markup to the cost including overhead, and enforces Minimum job once for the combined base subtotal. The
internal breakdown remains visible to you on Review quote.
Example with simple costs
Calculation
Labor + Materials + Extras
$1,000 direct cost
Overhead at 12%
$120; internal cost including overhead = $1,120
Markup at 24% of $1,120
$268.80
Base selling subtotal
$1,388.80, assuming the minimum is lower
Custom charge of $100
$1,488.80 final total if no override and stored tax is zero
The displayed Profit is the calculated markup amount. It does not automatically include any additional uplift caused
by Minimum job or custom items. A 24% markup is not a 24% selling-price margin.
Stored assumptions and tax
The engine supports a stored tax percentage, but the current Rates screen has no tax editor and starter tax is 0%.
Custom items are added after the calculated base total; the app does not automatically apply overhead, markup, or
additional tax to them. Review any required tax handling using your business process.
Crew-hours versus workdays
Crew-hours represent total labor effort. Ten crew-hours can mean one person working ten hours or two people
working five hours each. On review, set Crew size and Hours / day to estimate duration.
Workdays = crew-hours / (crew size x hours/day), rounded up to the next half day, with a minimum of half a day. For
17 crew-hours, two workers, and 8 hours/day: 17 / 16 = 1.0625, displayed as 1.5 workdays.
Duration is a labor-based estimate. It does not automatically schedule cure time, drying intervals, supplier lead
times, weather delays, or inspections. Explain those separately in Customer notes and do not promise a calendar
completion date from this number alone.
WZXU FIELDQUOTE  /  DETAILED USER GUIDE
October 1, 2026  |  Workspace edition
10 / 16

title: Adjust the quote before export
text:
USER GUIDE / 10
Adjust the quote before export
Custom charges and discounts
1. Under Adjust before sending, enter a descriptive Custom item label and its dollar Amount.
2. Use a positive amount for a charge or a negative amount for a discount. Select Add custom item; typing in the
builder alone does not add it.
3. Check the listed item and total. Remove an item with its trash button when necessary. The visible custom items
appear on the customer PDF.
Manual total overrides
Typing in Override total creates a manual final selling total. When a manual total exists, it replaces the calculated
total plus all custom items. Custom item rows still appear on the PDF, so verify that the visible scope amounts and
final total communicate your intended pricing.
Scenario
Displayed final total
Calculated total $2,000; custom
charge +$150; no override
$2,150
Same quote with Override total
set to $2,100
$2,100
Add a -$100 discount while that
override remains
$2,100; the manual total still controls
No visible reset button: blanking Override total is interpreted as zero, not as removing the override. If you need
automatic pricing after creating a manual total, start a new estimate and re-enter the scope. A duplicate retains the
override. Always inspect the Manual override line under How WZXU FieldQuote calculated it.
Notes, terms, and exclusions
Write Customer notes to identify locations, inclusions, material specifications, allowances, and scheduling
assumptions. These notes are customer-visible. Avoid placing private margins or internal commentary there.
Edit Payment terms on this quote. The entered text is saved with the estimate and included on the PDF; leave it
blank to omit the section. Include the deposit, balance trigger, and any agreed payment schedule clearly.
The PDF also prints stored exclusions. Fresh estimates include an exclusion for hidden damage, permits, and
unlisted work. The current review screen has no exclusions editor. If you include a permit allowance or other
potentially conflicting item, clarify its exact inclusion in notes and inspect the PDF for contradictory wording.
WZXU FIELDQUOTE  /  DETAILED USER GUIDE
October 1, 2026  |  Workspace edition

title: Create and send the customer PDF
text:
USER GUIDE / 11
Create and send the customer PDF
1. After measurement changes, select Review price again. Verify the calculated scope and saved costs.
2. Check the customer, site, title, expiry date, final total, duration, custom items, notes, and payment terms.
3. Select Create PDF quote. The app saves the quote first. If saving fails, it reports an error and does not create a
PDF.
4. Locate the downloaded file. In the Windows app, choose a destination when prompted. The filename uses the
quote number and customer name.
5. Open the PDF and review all pages before attaching it to your email or message. Set Status to Sent yourself after
sending.
What is included
The PDF contains company contact details, quote number and expiry, customer and site, work-area scope groups
and selling line amounts, customer-visible custom items, estimated total and workdays, notes and exclusions,
nonblank payment terms, and customer signature/date lines.
Internal labor costs, overhead, markup, rate snapshots, and calibration records are not included as private
breakdowns. Scope descriptions are concise and do not list every trade option; use Customer notes for important
conditions and specifications.
Pre-send checklist
Check
What to confirm
Identity and scope
Correct company, customer, site, area count, and unambiguous location notes.
Quantity and assumptions
Correct feet versus inches, base area versus coated area, no unintended duplicated
areas or allowances.
Price consistency
Expected total; manual override understood; custom charges and discounts present; no
unexplained mismatch in line amounts.
Terms and exclusions
Payment schedule correct; expiry current; included allowances do not conflict with
exclusion wording.
Presentation
All pages readable; no clipped long names or addresses; no sample watermark on a
real quote.
Create PDF quote downloads a document; it does not email it, record acceptance, collect a signature, or take
payment. The printed signature lines are blank lines. Windows File > Print prints the current app window; use the
exported quote PDF for customer delivery.
WZXU FIELDQUOTE  /  DETAILED USER GUIDE
October 1, 2026  |  Workspace edition
12 / 16

title: Manage saved quotes and examples
text:
USER GUIDE / 12
Manage saved quotes and examples
Find and reopen an estimate
Open Estimates. Search by customer name, project title, or quote number; use Status to filter the list. Select a record
to open Review quote. Use the back arrow for measurements and then job details. After changes to measurements,
select Review price before creating a replacement PDF.
Use statuses as your own tracking labels
Status
Suggested use
Draft
Work is still being measured or priced.
Ready
Checked and prepared for sending. Save as ready explicitly changes the status.
Sent
You have sent the exported quote externally.
Accepted / Declined
Record the customer's response yourself.
Archived
Keep the record while filtering it out of active work.
These labels are manual. Creating a PDF does not automatically set Sent. Accepted does not trigger an electronic
signature or payment workflow. Archived records remain stored and searchable.
Duplicate or delete
The plus action next to a saved estimate creates a copy with a new quote number, Draft status, and "Copy of" title. It
retains measurements, saved rates, custom items, payment terms, and any manual total. Review inherited customer
details and expiration. A copy is useful for similar work but is not a reprice using current rates.
The trash action asks for confirmation before deleting the estimate. There is no in-app undo. Prefer Archived if you
need to retain the quote, and keep a backup before removing records.
Practice with six examples
In Settings, select Load six examples or Refresh six examples. These are fictional jobs, marked Example in the
app and SAMPLE - NOT A REAL QUOTE on exported PDFs. Refresh replaces example records; Remove examples
removes demo records after confirmation.
Ordinary JSON backups exclude demo estimates and demo customers. Duplicating an example creates an
ordinary Draft copy that is included in backups and no longer has the sample marking. Replace all fictional
information before treating that copy as a real quote.
WZXU FIELDQUOTE  /  DETAILED USER GUIDE
October 1, 2026  |  Workspace edition
13 / 16

title: Back up, restore, and move records
text:
USER GUIDE / 13
Back up, restore, and move records
Download a portable backup
1. Let your latest edits save, then open Settings > Download JSON backup.
2. Save the date-stamped .json file in a location you can find. Keep a second copy away from the device, especially
before changing computers or browsers.
3. Keep customer PDFs separately for your sent-quote history. A PDF is a customer document, not a restorable app
backup.
Normal backup includes
Normal backup excludes
Ordinary estimates, saved rate books, company profile, and
ordinary customer records.
Demo examples and demo customers; completed-job
calibration records and comparisons.
Restore on another app copy
1. Download a backup of the destination app first if it already has important data.
2. Open Settings > Restore backup, select the original FieldQuote JSON file, and wait for Backup restored.
3. Reload or reopen the app before checking Rates and company information. The restore operation refreshes the
estimate list, but restored settings may not be reflected in the current screen state until a reload.
4. Confirm expected estimates, customer details, rates, and company profile. Open an estimate and inspect its saved
pricing snapshot.
Restore merges records by their internal IDs. Matching IDs are overwritten; unrelated existing records remain. It is not
a clean replacement and not automatic synchronization. Restore accepts the app's supported backup versions;
editing the JSON manually can cause failed or inconsistent restores.
Portable Windows moves
Close FieldQuote, then copy the entire Portable folder including Data to the new writable location. This carries the full
local profile rather than only the normal backup subset. Preserve Data when updating portable application files.
Browser storage can be cleared, and each browser profile or app copy has its own local data. No account or cloud
record synchronization is included. The supplied portable release does not encrypt its data; protect access to the
folder, device, and backups.
WZXU FIELDQUOTE  /  DETAILED USER GUIDE
October 1, 2026  |  Workspace edition
14 / 16

title: Calibrate against completed jobs
text:
USER GUIDE / 14
Calibrate against completed jobs
1. Open Rates > Calibrate with completed jobs. Select Painting, Concrete, or Windows.
2. Enter Completed job name and the original measurements and job conditions. Use the same measured scope as
the finished job.
3. Enter Actual quantity, Actual crew-hours, Material spend, and Crew size. Quantity is square feet for
painting/concrete or units for windows; it is not gallons or concrete yards.
4. Open Equipment and extra costs for Equipment, Disposal, and Subcontractors. Enter Quoted price, Approved
price, Final price, Change orders, and Unexpected work as available.
5. Select Compare with WZXU FieldQuote. A job name and positive actual quantity, crew-hours, and final price are
required to enable this action.
Interpret the history
The comparison shows Quantity, Materials, Crew time, Internal cost, and selling-price variance. Variance is
(estimated - actual) / actual x 100. Positive means the app estimated above the actual result; negative means below
it. A zero actual value produces a displayed 0% rather than a meaningful percentage.
Example: estimated crew-hours of 12 compared with 10 actual hours gives +20%. The history emphasizes variances
above 15% in absolute value. Classify Largest cause as Needs review, Incorrect formula, Missing job input, Starter
rate, Rounding, or Job exception.
Improve assumptions carefully
Start with representative completed work, ideally one job in each trade you use. Investigate whether a difference
came from measurement, scope, supplier pricing, production, or an exception. Change relevant visible rates manually
and select Save rates for future estimates.
Calibration is a comparison worksheet. It does not automatically fit rates, reprice old estimates, or certify
accuracy. Comparisons use the rate values currently loaded in the Rates worksheet, including unsaved edits.
Save intended rate changes first for a consistent baseline.
Estimated internal cost includes overhead. The actual internal-cost comparator adds material spend, crew-hours at
the current labor rate, equipment, disposal, and subcontractors without separately adding actual overhead. Account
for that difference when interpreting the variance. Selling-price comparison uses Final price; quoted/approved prices
and change orders are recorded but do not replace it.
Calibration records stay local and are excluded from customer PDFs and normal JSON backups. The current screen
has no dedicated calibration export or record editor; retain your source job records separately.
WZXU FIELDQUOTE  /  DETAILED USER GUIDE
October 1, 2026  |  Workspace edition
15 / 16

title: Troubleshooting and daily reference
text:
USER GUIDE / 15
Troubleshooting and daily reference
Problem
Practical response
Estimates seem missing
Check the same browser profile, app copy, and website origin. Browser, installed, and
portable records are separate. Restore a known backup if needed.
New rates did not change an old
quote
Expected: that quote retains its snapshot. Start a new estimate to use current rates; a
duplicate retains old rates.
Windows material cost is wrong
Check Unit allowance on the estimate and the size factor. Fresh quotes populate $420;
zero means zero material allowance.
Custom items do not change the
total
Inspect Manual override. An active override controls the final total. Blank override
becomes zero.
Painting gallons look too high
Check measurement mode, base area, coats, ceiling duplication, openings in sq ft,
duplicated work areas, and gallons override.
Concrete extras look too high
Each area can add delivery, short-load, and pumping. Check base-preparation overlaps
and supplier allowances.
Review price is disabled
Check and correct unusual painting quantities, then use I checked this unusual quantity
only after verification.
PDF did not download
Read the displayed save/export error. Retry after confirming storage and download
location. A failed save prevents PDF creation.
Restore failed or settings look
old
Use an original supported .json backup. After successful restore, reload to refresh
Rates and company profile.
Portable app cannot save
Extract the ZIP; keep portable.json and all app files together; move the full folder to a
writable location.
Offline first launch fails
Connect online and finish loading the app. Caching must complete before offline use.
A daily operating habit
